verses.1: After these events, the word of the LORD came to Abram in a vision, saying, "Do not fear, Abram. I am your shield, and your reward will be exceedingly great."
verses.2: Abram said, "O Lord GOD, what will you give me, since I continue childless, and the heir of my household is Eliezer of Damascus?"
verses.3: Abram added, "You have given me no offspring, and so a servant born in my house will inherit me."
verses.4: But the word of the LORD came to him, "This one will not inherit you. No, the one who will come from your own body will inherit you."
verses.5: He took him outside and said, "Look now toward the heavens and count the stars, if you are able to count them." He said to him, "So shall your offspring be."
verses.6: Abram believed the LORD, and he counted it to him as righteousness.
verses.7: He said to him, "I am the LORD who brought you from Ur of the Chaldeans to give you this land to possess it."
verses.8: Abram asked, "O Lord GOD, by what will I know that I will possess it?"
verses.9: He said to him, "Take for me a heifer three years old, a female goat three years old, a ram three years old, a turtledove, and a young pigeon."
verses.10: Abram took all these, cut them in two, and placed each half opposite the other. But he did not cut the birds.
verses.11: Birds of prey descended on the carcasses, and Abram drove them away.
verses.12: The sun was about to set, and a deep sleep fell upon Abram. A dark and terrifying shadow passed over him.
verses.13: He said to Abram, "Know this for certain: your descendants will be strangers in a land not theirs. They will serve and be oppressed there for four hundred years.
verses.14: But I will judge the nation they serve, and afterward they will go out with great possessions.
verses.15: As for you, you will go to your fathers in peace. You will be buried at a good old age."
verses.16: But in the fourth generation they will return here, for the sin of the Amorites is not yet complete."
verses.17: The sun had set, and it was dark. A smoking furnace and a flaming torch passed between the pieces.
verses.18: On that day the LORD made a covenant with Abram, saying, "To your offspring I give this land, from the river of Egypt to the great river, the Euphrates:
verses.19: the Kenite, the Kenezzite, and the Kadmonite,
verses.20: the Hittite, the Perizzite, and the Rephaim,
verses.21: the Amorite, the Canaanite, the Girgashite, and the Jebusite."

notes:
Notes
- v. 8: "By what will I know" — the use of "בַּמָּה" is idiomatic, often rendered as "by what" or "in what way."
- v. 16: "the sin of the Amorites is not yet complete" — the Hebrew uses "עֲוֺן" (iniquity/sin) and "שָׁלֵם" (complete/satisfied), indicating a moral or judicial delay.
- v. 17: "a smoking furnace and a flaming torch passed between the pieces" — the imagery is poetic and symbolic, representing the seal of the covenant.
raw:
[1] After these events, the word of the LORD came to Abram in a vision, saying, "Do not fear, Abram. I am your shield, and your reward will be exceedingly great."

[2] Abram said, "O Lord GOD, what will you give me, since I continue childless, and the heir of my household is Eliezer of Damascus?"

[3] Abram added, "You have given me no offspring, and so a servant born in my house will inherit me."

[4] But the word of the LORD came to him, "This one will not inherit you. No, the one who will come from your own body will inherit you."

[5] He took him outside and said, "Look now toward the heavens and count the stars, if you are able to count them." He said to him, "So shall your offspring be."

[6] Abram believed the LORD, and he counted it to him as righteousness.

[7] He said to him, "I am the LORD who brought you from Ur of the Chaldeans to give you this land to possess it."

[8] Abram asked, "O Lord GOD, by what will I know that I will possess it?"

[9] He said to him, "Take for me a heifer three years old, a female goat three years old, a ram three years old, a turtledove, and a young pigeon."

[10] Abram took all these, cut them in two, and placed each half opposite the other. But he did not cut the birds.

[11] Birds of prey descended on the carcasses, and Abram drove them away.

[12] The sun was about to set, and a deep sleep fell upon Abram. A dark and terrifying shadow passed over him.

[13] He said to Abram, "Know this for certain: your descendants will be strangers in a land not theirs. They will serve and be oppressed there for four hundred years.

[14] But I will judge the nation they serve, and afterward they will go out with great possessions.

[15] As for you, you will go to your fathers in peace. You will be buried at a good old age."

[16] But in the fourth generation they will return here, for the sin of the Amorites is not yet complete."

[17] The sun had set, and it was dark. A smoking furnace and a flaming torch passed between the pieces.

[18] On that day the LORD made a covenant with Abram, saying, "To your offspring I give this land, from the river of Egypt to the great river, the Euphrates:

[19] the Kenite, the Kenezzite, and the Kadmonite,

[20] the Hittite, the Perizzite, and the Rephaim,

[21] the Amorite, the Canaanite, the Girgashite, and the Jebusite."

---
Notes
- v. 8: "By what will I know" — the use of "בַּמָּה" is idiomatic, often rendered as "by what" or "in what way."
- v. 16: "the sin of the Amorites is not yet complete" — the Hebrew uses "עֲוֺן" (iniquity/sin) and "שָׁלֵם" (complete/satisfied), indicating a moral or judicial delay.
- v. 17: "a smoking furnace and a flaming torch passed between the pieces" — the imagery is poetic and symbolic, representing the seal of the covenant.
